### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c523d0100e9368ba8af3b08c652f23e943de46a`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c523d0100e9368ba8af3b08c652f23e943de46a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `760e9a9734fca1f91bb43729e106d03c6d59e28c` — the merge of head `67affbcd18a6bab65645e73a5c707e1bc171869f` into base `2c523d0100e9368ba8af3b08c652f23e943de46a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 760e9a9734fca1f91bb43729e106d03c6d59e28c && git checkout 760e9a9734fca1f91bb43729e106d03c6d59e28c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2c523d0100e9368ba8af3b08c652f23e943de46a 67affbcd18a6bab65645e73a5c707e1bc171869f && git checkout -B drift-repro 2c523d0100e9368ba8af3b08c652f23e943de46a && git merge --no-ff 67affbcd18a6bab65645e73a5c707e1bc171869f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c523d0100e9368ba8af3b08c652f23e943de46a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2c523d0100e9368ba8af3b08c652f23e943de46a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `67affbcd18a6bab65645e73a5c707e1bc171869f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/feature-gate-guard.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-team.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-team-member.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-team-add-member-action.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/platform-objects.test.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/public-feature-registry.test.ts, .changeset/25337-spec-book-team-add-member.md

PR #25670 (draft, author objectstack-fleet[bot]) at the head above, read against origin/main at 2c523d01 (the PR's base; merge base baae6ed1). Face: published schema (a non-test file under packages/spec/src), read off the committed file list. Inputs: card #25337 with all eight of its comments, the PR body and its one comment, the file list, the net diff (10 files, 137 insertions, 0 deletions) and the head's check-runs. The rest of the diff (the `sys_team` action, its test, the four generated bundles, the lowering-matrix row and the platform-objects changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The one row, in the one place.** `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.organization.gatedInputs` gains exactly `'sys_team.actions.add_team_member'` at line 126, immediately after `'sys_team.actions.remove_team'` (line 125) and before `'sys_team_member.actions.add_team_member'` (line 127); the file's net diff is one added line and nothing removed. This is what rulings 6370058183 (「补一行 spec，删除半张不做」, A + C) and 6384716955 (「维持 旧裁决 A + C」, with the placement and the same-PR requirement) ask for. **Right.**
2. **The membership-list row is untouched.** `'sys_team_member.actions.add_team_member'` stands unchanged on line 127, and `sys-team-member.object.ts` is not in the diff. **Right.**
3. **No delete half.** `sys_team.remove_team` is byte-identical (no `disabled`, no reason text), no reason key enters `action.zod.ts`, no registry row names a delete, and `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` is not in the file list, so `allowRemovingAllTeams` stays unset. Ruling C holds. **Right.**
4. **What the row claims resolves, and the gate reads it in both directions.** `sys-team.object.ts` declares `add_team_member` on `sys_team` with `requiresFeature: 'organization'` and `requiresMembershipReach: 'add_team_member'`; `lowerRequiresFeature` composes the gate last, and the lowering-matrix row added to `platform-objects.test.ts` pins the lowered `visible` as the grade term followed by `features.organization != false` as a top-level conjunct, the same shape as the three sibling `sys_team` rows. So `feature-gate-guard.test.ts`'s forward leg (the registry row resolves to an action carrying the gate conjunct) and its reverse leg (every `features.organization` reference is booked) both hold on this head, and neither could hold with the row and the action in separate PRs, which is why both are here. The walker's floor (at least 37 referenced inputs) only rises. **Right.**
5. **Grammar and registry invariants.** The path matches the spec test's object-dot-actions-dot-action regex and the guard's resolver regex; the flag count stays 12 (`PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURE_NAMES` unchanged, so the `requiresFeature` enum is unchanged); `organization` still declares `gatedInputs` and no `exempt`; the plugin-auth drift guard (`public-feature-registry.test.ts`) compares served flag names and reads `semantics` only, never `gatedInputs`, so the served `/api/v1/auth/config` contract does not move. **Right.**
6. **Placement versus declaration order.** The object declares `add_team_member` between `update_team` and `remove_team`; the registry row sits after `remove_team`. No reader of `gatedInputs` reads order (the forward leg is an `it.each` over rows, the reverse leg a `Set`, the spec test checks grammar and the gatedInputs-or-exempt exclusion), and the ruling fixes the position by name. **Right.**
7. **Public surface.** The published constant is `as const`, so its literal tuple type gains one member; the declared entry type (`gatedInputs?: readonly string[]`), every export, every schema and every authorable key are unchanged, and `gatedInputs` is a census the completeness guard reads, not an accept set that admits or refuses authored metadata. Additive; nothing published narrows. **Right**, and it is what makes the `Clause-②: no` line below true.
8. **Serial neighbours.** Open PR #25626 adds `'sys_user.actions.create_user.params.organizationId'` and open PR #25661 moves `'sys_organization.actions.rename_organization'` into the `organization` block of the same file; neither has merged, and origin/main is still this PR's base. Different rows, so the later landing merges main and the guard re-runs, as the PR body says; `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` is green. Not blocking.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/25337-spec-book-team-add-member.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the same two lines at line start. **Right.** `Metadata-protocol: none` is true (no key, accepted value, enum member, metadata type, default or meaning that an author can write changes: `requiresFeature: 'organization'` was accepted before and is accepted identically after), and under the level rule `none` takes `patch`. `Clause-②: no` is true by its definition (no published accept set or public surface widens, and nothing narrows, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed): item 7 above. Precedent agrees: the `sys_organization.invite_user` booking shipped as a spec `patch` under `Clause-②: no`.
- Not `skip-changeset`: both `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` publish, and each has its patch changeset. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- The second changeset (`@objectstack/platform-objects`: `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`) is the lane seat's; read only for consistency with the spec row, it is consistent (a new action row on a platform object is shipped metadata, not a new authorable key).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **PR author** is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; nothing to note.
- **Dev flag, os-dev report 6385318010 `open_questions`, the commit-trailer conflict** (the dispatch text asked for a model-named co-author trailer; AGENTS.md and the pre-push hook refuse a model identifier in that pair). **Answered: the repository rule holds, and the head already complies.** All five commits on the head carry `Claude-Session:` and the model-free `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer at the anthropic noreply address, read off the commit trailers; AGENTS.md's own exemption treats even a harness-written model-named trailer as a reporting matter, not a deviation. Nothing to escalate for this PR; the dispatch template's wording is the dispatching seat's to fix, outside this record.
- **Dev flag, PR body "Acceptance notes"**: `public-feature-registry.test.ts` was not run locally and is declared to CI Test Core. Read in the cited code: it reads flag names and `semantics`, never `gatedInputs`, so this row cannot move it; Test Core is named below as pending.
- **Dev flag, PR body serial note**: covered in ① item 8; accepted.
- **Card flags**: both earlier `open_questions` (report 6364672577) were ruled A + C and confirmed; the diff implements A and omits the delete half per C. No open flag remains on the card.
- **Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-24T14:30Z**: green — Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three Lint · scoped lanes, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Check Documentation Links, Auto Label, filter, and the four claim guards; skipped by path filter or opt-in — Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, the Dogfood matrix shards, 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke; **still pending** — Test Core (1/6) through (6/6), Type Check · workspace; **red — none.** The verdict below stands on the diff; the landing still waits for every check to finish green, per the queue rule.
- `needs:contract-review` is not on the PR (labels: documentation, size/m, tests, tooling); no label was touched by this record.
